messages:
elaine: quick question — deployment helper (ci->deploy) needs to enumerate projects under our org to find the target env. Do we have to grant org-level read (org.viewer) to the service account, or is there a safer least-priv path?

martin: you can avoid org-level viewer in most cases. if the CI flow already knows which project ids it might deploy to, grant project-level roles on those projects instead. what specific API calls is the job doing?

elaine: it calls the Resource Manager `projects.list` to fetch metadata and then decides. i was trying to avoid maintaining a manually curated list of projects.

jordan: two options: 1) keep central small mapping (pref + git ref) and give CI per-project service accounts permission to deploy, or 2) give a "discovery" SA org.viewer but scope it with a condition and narrow key rotation, or use short-lived impersonation. prefer option1 for least privilege.

sre-anna: agree with jordan. also watch logs: when we grant org-level list perms, Resource Manager responses can leak project names/labels. if any labels contain customer identifiers we need to redact before writing to logs. elasticsearch/Logstash pipelines should hash IDs.

elaine: good call — we do have some older projects that used customer slug in project-id. need guidance on redaction.

security-bot: FYI from policy: org-level viewer should be avoided for automated agents. If unavoidable, add an IAM condition limiting access to `resource.name` patterns and require key rotation <= 24h. See internal doc: https://redwood-internal.example/policies/iam-conditions

martin: practical pattern we've used: create a management project that stores an allowlist of active project ids (small table). CI queries that table (BigQuery or configs bucket) and then impersonates per-project SA to do deploys. no org-level role required.

elaine: that sounds good. if we go that route, what exact roles do we need on the target projects? just iam.serviceAccountUser + deployer role?

devops: usually: (a) grant the CI runner SA roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator or allow impersonation via workloads; (b) grant a scoped deploy role on the target (e.g. roles/clouddeploy.deployor or a custom role limited to what's needed). avoid broad roles/editor.

jordan: example gcloud flow:
```
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=/secrets/ci-sa.json
gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate --impersonate-service-account=proj-deploy-sa@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=management-project
# then run deployment commands against target project
```

elaine: thanks. last Q — temporary emergency access: if SRE needs to list org projects during an incident, do we have a JIT pattern?

security-bot: yes — use the Just-In-Time access service: raise a short-lived access ticket, get approval from oncall+sec, and grant time-bound org.viewer via the access-automation. All grants get logged and audited. Link: https://redwood-internal.example/jit

sre-anna: and redact incident attachments: never paste raw project ids that map to customers in public channels. use internal ticket only.

elaine: perfect. i'll prototype the management-project allowlist + impersonation approach and file a quick runbook. thanks all :thumbsup:
